outline.chapter_title: Procedural Posture and the Extraordinary Nature of Interim Relief
outline.description: This chapter establishes the complex procedural history of the case, detailing the sequence of executive actions, district court injunctions, and prior appellate stays. It explains why the Ninth Circuit issued an interlocutory order rather than a final merits opinion and defines the specific legal mechanism of a 'stay pending appeal' under Federal Rule of Appellate Procedure 8.
subtopics: Timeline of Executive Orders 14163 and 14169 versus District Court Preliminary Injunctions
The Evolution of Appellate Stays: From Partial Grants to Administrative Stays
The Function and Legal Standard of a Stay Pending Appeal vs. Final Judgment
Expedited Review and the Decision to Issue an Order Prior to Merits Opinion

outline.chapter_title: Presidential Authority Over Entry: Analyzing 8 U.S.C. § 1182(f)
outline.description: This chapter examines the first major legal issue addressed by the panel: the President's power to suspend refugee admissions. It details the court's application of *Trump v. Hawaii* to determine that the government demonstrated a likelihood of success on the merits regarding the suspension of entry, focusing on the deferential standard applied to presidential findings of detriment to national interests.
subtopics: Statutory Text of 8 U.S.C. § 1182(f): The 'Detrimental to Interests' Prerequisite
The Doctrine of Deference in Immigration Policy: Lessons from *Trump v. Hawaii*
Application of the 'Likelihood of Success' Factor to the Suspension of USRAP
Why the Challenge to Entry Suspension Failed at the Stay Stage

outline.chapter_title: Mandatory Duties in Refugee Resettlement: Interpreting 8 U.S.C. § 1522
outline.description: This chapter explores the pivotal turning point in the opinion where the court distinguishes between suspending entry and defunding domestic services. It provides a close reading of 8 U.S.C. § 1522, analyzing how statutory commands like 'shall' and specific appropriations create a mandatory duty for the government to provide reception and placement services, contrasting this with the discretionary nature of entry restrictions.
subtopics: Statutory Construction of § 1522: Distinguishing 'Authorization' from 'Mandate'
The Significance of Congressional Appropriations in Creating Enforceable Duties
Specific Mandatory Provisions: Unaccompanied Minors and Cash/Medical Assistance
The Gap Between Statutory Obligation and Executive Action: Termination of Cooperative Agreements

outline.chapter_title: Balancing Equities and Crafting Tailored Remedial Relief
outline.description: This chapter analyzes how the court applied the four-factor *Nken* test to reach a split outcome. It explains why irreparable harm and public interest favored reinstating service agreements despite the stay on entry restrictions, and details the specific scope of the relief ordered—limiting reinstatement only to agreements necessary for already-admitted refugees.
subtopics: Applying the Four-Factor Test (*Nken v. Holder*) to Mixed Questions of Law
Irreparable Injury to Refugees Already Admitted Versus Those Seeking Entry
Public Interest Considerations: Domestic Stability vs. Foreign Policy Discretion
The Scope of the Remedy: Reinstating Cooperative Agreements Under § 1522(b)(1)(A)(ii)

outline.chapter_title: Judicial Dissent on Statutory Interpretation: The Debate Over Discretionary Funding
outline.description: This chapter dissects Judge Lee's partial dissent, which challenges the majority's interpretation of § 1522 as mandatory. It highlights the textualist arguments regarding section titles ('Authorization'), qualifying phrases ('to the extent of available appropriations', 'if necessary', 'as needed'), and the separation of powers concerns inherent in judicially mandating executive spending programs.
subtopics: Textualist Arguments: The Significance of Section Titles and Permissive Language
Interpreting Qualifiers: 'If Necessary,' 'As Needed,' and 'Available Appropriations'
Separation of Powers Concerns in Judicial Management of Executive Programs
The Practical Implications of Viewing § 1522 as Purely Discretionary
